observations: Independently viewed all 12 baseline and candidate PNGs at their native dimensions: paired full stage images and same-frame ear detail crops for adult support, child recovery head view, and infant contrast head view.

The adult supporting-hand view shows a clear localized improvement: the lower/right end of the raised outer ridge now blends into a rounded lobe, reducing the previous stacked-disc appearance. The upper helix remains visible.

The child ear is small and partly hidden by the skull in the native head view. Its lower outline looks slightly less layered, without a visible gap, spike, or new shading defect. This pair mainly verifies the child recovery pose.
The infant contrast pair retains its continuous white ear and head silhouette. Surface relief is not appreciably distinguishable at this size and contrast setting.

Across the three pairs, framing, supporting hands, face, clothing, and surrounding stage appear unchanged. The adult ear still reads as a shallow oval relief, so this improves the lobe transition rather than completing anatomical realism.
limitations: Three matched raw-module browser views were visually reviewed. Small child and high-contrast infant ear crops reveal limited surface detail. Full application loading, production builds, and deployment were not tested.
